resources.string: When the TV\'s original launcher comes to the front, brings back the Home screen. Only checks which app is in front, without reading what is on the screen.
Wallpaper: fixed gradient, choose a photo source
Only one photo available for now
Move with the arrows, then press OK
Leave the field empty to go back to the original name, “%1$s”.
The folder takes the place of “%1$s” on Home, with the app inside.
“%1$s” leaves Home for the folder you choose.
Checked apps are in “%1$s”; the others stay on Home.
The folder goes away; its apps return to Home in its place.
Deleting a preinstalled app needs local debugging. Press Start: the TV shows “Allow USB debugging?”. Check “Always allow”, then choose “Allow”.
This app is preinstalled on the TV. Once deleted, it no longer appears on Home and no longer runs in the background. You can restore it in Home Settings → Apps → Deleted Preinstalled Apps.
This app is a home screen that can take over if this one has a problem. Without it, the TV will have no backup home screen if this one does not start. The app and its data will be deleted.
The app and its data will be deleted.
A child profile asks for a PIN to switch profiles, open settings or delete an app. No PIN is set yet.
Each profile has its own Home: app order, hidden apps, folders and wallpaper. Create one in “Manage Profiles…”.
“%1$s” is a child profile: first choose the PIN that will let you leave it (%2$d to %3$d digits).
To go straight to the channel, allow local debugging (Home Settings → System).
Local debugging must be allowed once. Press Start: the TV shows “Allow USB debugging?”. Check “Always allow”, then choose “Allow”.
In the window that appears, check “Always allow”, then choose “Allow”
Done: Turn Off and Free Up Memory are now available
Permission denied; try again in Home Settings
Lyrics unavailable: LRCLIB can\'t be reached
No synced lyrics for this track
The TV turns off completely. Turn it back on with the power button on the remote.
Press OK on a control to move it, resize it or remove it. Press Back when you are done.
Page %1$d: add a control to it, or delete it.
Another control is in that spot.
Not enough room here for that size: move the control first.
Control Center keeps at least one control.
It takes the first free spot on this page, or else on another page, or else on a new page.
No room left: remove a control or make one smaller.
The controls go back to their original place and size, on two pages.
Each checked input becomes an icon on Home: one press switches to it.
Location detected from the TV\'s IP address. To choose another city, use the Phone Page (Settings tab).
The forecast will show here as soon as the TV receives it. This needs an Internet connection.
canvasOS needs the “Nearby devices” permission to show your Bluetooth devices and connect one. It is used for nothing else: the TV does not search for any device.
The TV\'s Bluetooth is off. Turn it on in the TV\'s settings.
No paired devices. Pair one in the TV\'s Bluetooth settings.
Turn on the controller: it reconnects by itself.
This TV does not let canvasOS connect “%1$s”. Do it in the TV\'s Bluetooth settings.
This TV does not let canvasOS disconnect “%1$s”. Do it in the TV\'s Bluetooth settings.
The TV is about to go to sleep. Cancel the timer to keep watching.
Press Start: the TV shows “Allow USB debugging?”. Check “Always allow”, then choose “Allow”.
The clock, the Dock, the profile picture, the weather, the focus effect, Control Center (its style and controls) and the boot animation.
The Home screen background and how often it changes, and the photo frame the TV shows as its screen saver.
The content of the app selected in the Dock, full screen above it, and where it comes from.
The Control Center player for what apps are playing, and the notification banners at the top right of the screen.
Freeing up memory, in sleep, on a schedule or right now, the apps it spares, and what the power button does.
Apps hidden from Home, deleted preinstalled apps, and folders.
A Home screen for each person, with their apps, folders and wallpaper; a child profile is protected by a PIN.
A web page for a phone on the same Wi-Fi: remote with keyboard, photos and image links, app installs. Its QR code and its protection.
Remote buttons linked to canvasOS functions on Home: single or long press, the button learned by pressing it; on a set-top box, channel numbers.
Local and ADB debugging, the TV\'s address, Home Guard, the TV\'s own settings, canvasOS updates and its version.
The time on the Home screen and in Control Center, in 12-hour (11:49 AM) or 24-hour (23:49) format.
A small clock at the top right, or a large clock with the date at the top left (the old style), or none.
Recents: the app you open moves to the front, as it does now. Fixed: the order you chose with “Edit Home” is kept.

The profile picture at the top right of Home: the initial of its name on its color, or a photo imported from the Phone Page. Press it to switch profiles. It stays visible while there is more than one profile.

The temperature and conditions next to the clock, and the five-day forecast in Control Center. They come from Open-Meteo and update every 30 minutes while Home is shown. Until a city is chosen, the location is guessed once from the TV\'s public IP address (ip-api.com).
To choose another city: the Phone Page (Settings tab, Weather section), or a computer with the CONFIG command (weather_city).
tvOS: the selected app grows, tilts with the direction, and a shine passes over it. Simple: it only grows.\nAuto picks Simple on low-power TVs.
Glass: frosted glass that shows the picture behind it; the selected button turns white. Panel: the old dark panel.\nAuto picks Glass on all TVs.

Opens Control Center in edit mode. Its controls sit on a 4 × 6 grid, on up to three pages (Down from the last row goes to the next page). OK on a control: move it, resize it, remove it, add a control or a page. Back to finish. Elsewhere, a long press on OK on the Control Center button, at the top right of Home, does the same.
Puts the Control Center controls back in their original place and size, on two pages.
The controls go back to their original place and size, on two pages.
The built-in title card and boot film: canvasOS\'s, or Apple TV\'s (tvOS). They serve as the icon of these settings and as the boot animation, unless chosen otherwise below.
The icon of these settings, on Home and at the top of this page: the title card of the chosen logo, your own picture imported from the Phone Page, or the built-in gear.
Plays the first time Home appears after the TV turns on; at the end, the logo grows and opens Home. Press any button to skip it.

Film of the chosen logo: canvasOS\'s or Apple TV\'s, per the Logo row. Imported Video: your own, from the Phone Page, whose final logo grows and opens Home. canvasOS Name: the name fades in, then grows.
\nNo video imported yet: the chosen logo\'s film plays instead.

When waking from sleep, the screen stays black this long before the animation. Many TVs (especially OLED) only show a picture a few seconds after turning on: make it longer if the start of the animation is missing, shorter if the black lasts too long.
Plays the sound of the animation film or video.
Goes back to Home and plays it once now.
The Home screen background: a theme, a wallpaper source, or your own photos.
How often the automatic wallpaper changes. Never: the photo only changes with the Next Photo button in Control Center (or Change Now below).
Gets a new photo from the wallpaper source. Photos are downloaded when they are shown; old ones are deleted after a few days.
After a while with no activity, the TV shows photos or aerials full screen, instead of its own screen saver.
The photo frame shows the wallpaper photos, or Apple TV aerials.
Time with no activity before the photo frame appears.
How long each photo shows in the photo frame.

The content of the app selected in the Dock, full screen above it. Full: the “Continue Watching” row published for Android TV, then TMDB trends (with your key) and web sources. Android TV Only: no TMDB or web. Off: the wallpaper stays visible.
The row apps (YouTube, Netflix…) publish for Android TV: what you were watching, to pick up again. When off, Top Shelf only uses TMDB and web sources, when the Top Shelf mode allows them.
Choose “Add Shortcut…”, the function, then press the remote button that will do it.
Press to change the button or the function, or delete this shortcut. Shortcuts work on Home, not in other apps.

The function first, then the button: a short press links it to a single press, a held press to a long press. The TV\'s buttons (Home, Volume) and those Home uses (arrows, OK, Back on a single press) are refused.

On by default. On Home, type a channel number (up to three digits): live TV opens on that channel. A digit linked to a shortcut keeps its shortcut. Going straight to the channel needs local debugging; without it, live TV opens on the current channel.

Off by default. The remote\'s Settings and Profile buttons (and a few others: Guide, Input, TV) are taken by the TV before they reach canvasOS. When on, the canvasOS accessibility service (the one Home Guard uses) filters the buttons: it then sees every button pressed, in all apps, and keeps only those buttons, only on Home and only if they are linked; everything else passes through as is. Nothing is recorded. Needs local debugging once.
What the button will do; you choose the button next.
The app the button will open.
The input the button will switch to.
This TV does not give canvasOS access to its HDMI inputs (see AGENTS.md, section 9).
A short press links it to a single press, a held press to a long press. Back cancels.
The Settings and Profile buttons need “Capture TV Buttons”.
%1$s Try another button, or Back to cancel.

On by default. Shows in Control Center what an app is playing (title, artist, artwork) with play/pause and next track. To do this it reads the apps\' playback info (title, artist, artwork, playback state) through the notification listener; nothing is recorded.

On by default, with Now Playing. At the top left of Home, a capsule shows the artwork, title and artist of what an app is playing, with no controls: OK opens that app; play, pause and next track stay in Control Center. Nothing more is read for it.

On by default. For each new track, the TV asks LRCLIB (lrclib.net, free, no key) whether it has the lyrics: the title, artist, album and length of the track are sent, nothing else, and nothing is recorded. When it has them, a Lyrics button appears to the right of the Home player when the player is selected: OK shows the synced lyrics over the dimmed background (unsynced lyrics are not offered), OK again hides them. When off, nothing is sent to LRCLIB.
Where the lines appear on Home: on the left under the player, in the center, or on the right.

On by default. Shows app notifications at the top right (doorbell, messages, smart home…). The title and text of notifications from all apps, except excluded ones, are read, shown for 6 seconds and never recorded. When off, no notification is read.
Notifications from ticked apps are neither read nor shown. All others show as banners.
\nWithout permission to display over other apps (step 4), banners only appear on Home.
Notifications from ticked apps are neither read nor shown. Those from other apps show for 6 seconds at the top right.
Closes background apps when the TV goes to sleep, for a smoother restart. Apps playing sound or video, or running a service (casting, server), are spared.
Regularly closes background apps, except the app on screen and those playing sound or video or running a service.
Closes background apps now. Those playing sound or video, or running a service (casting, server), are spared.
Memory has not been freed up yet.
Apps that freeing up memory never closes, such as screen casting. Those playing sound or video, or running a service, are spared anyway while they do.
Sleep: as usual. Full Shutdown: saves energy, but startup takes longer.
Allow local debugging first to turn this on
Apps that do not show on the Home screen.
Preinstalled apps deleted from the long-press menu; you can restore them here.
The folders on Home and their apps. You create and manage them on Home, with a long press on an app or a folder.
The profile whose Home screen is shown. Switch with the profile picture at the top right of Home.

Each profile has its own Home screen: the order of apps, hidden apps, folders, app names, pinned items and the wallpaper. Other settings apply to everyone. A child profile asks for the PIN to switch profiles, open Settings or delete an app.

Scan it with a phone on the same Wi-Fi. The page that opens works as a remote with a keyboard, imports photos and image links, sets the boot animation and the weather, and installs apps (APK). The remote and app installs need local debugging.
Changes the secret code in the address: phones that knew the old one can no longer use it and must scan again. Do this if a phone that opened the page is lost.
The code in the address is the only protection: anyone on the same network who knows it can control the TV. When off, the page does not respond at all.
Lets Home turn off the TV, free up memory and more through local debugging. In the window that appears, choose “Always Allow”.
Must be on for a computer to connect to the TV: without it, no installs or updates over the network. It is set in the TV\'s developer options.
Stops the system from turning off ADB debugging.
The TV\'s address on the local network. A computer on the same network uses it to connect (adb connect, port 5555), for example to install or update canvasOS.
When the Home button goes to the TV\'s original launcher, comes back here automatically.
The Home button now brings you here instead of the original launcher

Home Guard takes the Home button before the system does and opens Home directly, without showing the original launcher. It then sees every button pressed in all apps and keeps only the Home button. Turn it off if an app reacts twice to a button.

Looks for the latest canvasOS version on GitHub (Releases) and installs it in place: settings and permissions are kept. Press once to check, a second time to install. Installing needs local debugging. canvasOS also checks every day whether a new version exists, without downloading anything.
canvasOS, an Android TV home screen inspired by tvOS.
canvasOS %1$s is the latest released version.
canvasOS %1$s%2$s is available. Press OK to download and install it.
Installing goes through local debugging: allow it (the “Local Debugging” row above), then try again.
Freeing up memory does not close the ticked apps.
Ticked apps do not appear on the Home screen.
The folders on Home, in order, with the number of apps they show.

On Home, long-press an app: “New Folder…” puts it in a new folder, “Add to Folder…” in an existing one. Long-press a folder to rename it, add apps to it, move it or delete it; its apps then go back to Home.
Child profile: the PIN is asked for to leave it, open Settings or delete an app; “Hide” and “App Info” are not offered.
The main profile: the Home screen from before profiles. It cannot be deleted.
Press to rename it, change its color, make it a child profile or delete it.
One more profile, with its own Home screen. It starts with the default app order, no hidden apps or folders, and the main profile\'s wallpaper.
Asked for in a child profile to leave it, open Settings or delete an app. %1$d to %2$d digits; changing or removing it asks for the current code. If forgotten, remove it from a computer (adb).
A child profile is protected only once a PIN is set (the “PIN” row on this page).
Leave the field empty to go back to the name “%1$s”.
Its Home screen (app order, hidden apps, folders, names, wallpaper) is erased. The apps themselves stay installed.

Without a photo, the profile shows the initial of its name on its color.

From a phone: open the Phone Page (Home Settings → Phone Page), Settings tab, Profiles section, then “Change Photo”.

From a computer: adb push photo.jpg /sdcard/Android/data/%1$s/files/%2$s/%3$s.jpg
Child profiles will no longer be protected: anyone can leave them and open Settings without a code.
Choose an app to reinstall it from the system partition.

On the same Wi-Fi, scan the code with a phone\'s camera; the page stays available at any time. Remote and keyboard, photos and image links, boot animation, app installs (APK).\nThe code in the address is the only protection: regenerate it if a phone that opened the page is lost; phones that knew the old one will have to scan again.
%1$s: %2$s.\nWithout local debugging, only cached apps were stopped, and Android does not say which.
%1$s: %2$s.\nApps to keep, and those playing sound or video or running a service (casting, server), were not closed.
Choose the Home screen background. The photo frame uses the same source.

On the same Wi-Fi, scan the code with your phone\'s camera: import photos or add image links (one picture, a random-image API, a page or a JSON list of images). The TV fetches them every day. The same page is also your remote.
Unsplash needs a free key: scan the QR code on the right and paste it in the Settings tab
No photos yet: scan the QR code on the right with a phone to import some
No links yet: scan the QR code on the right with a phone to add some
This button is reserved for the TV.
Holding this button already does something on the Home screen.
This button is already used on the Home screen.
This button is already used on the Home screen: hold it to bind a long press.
The PIN must have %1$d to %2$d digits.
The two PINs did not match. Try again.
The TV has a new address (%1$s). canvasos.local still works; otherwise scan the QR code again in Home Settings → Phone Page.
The file to install cannot be found.
Local debugging is not responding: allow it in Home Settings → System.
The TV refuses installs through debugging (TCL TVs do this): install this app from the TV, with its file manager.
Another version of this app is already installed with a different signature: uninstall it first.
A newer version of this app is already installed.
This app needs a newer version of Android than the TV has.
This app is not built for this TV\'s processor.
The TV does not have enough storage left.
This file is not a valid APK, or it is incomplete.
The Phone Page is off (Home Settings → Phone Page).
The TV is not connected to a network. Connect it, then open this page again.
The Phone Page could not start: port %1$d may be in use by another app.
GitHub shows no public canvasOS Release (private repository, or no Release yet).
GitHub is limiting requests from this network: try again in an hour.
GitHub denies access to the Releases (private repository?).
GitHub cannot be reached: check the TV\'s internet connection.
The Release version \"%1$s\" cannot be read.
The link to %1$s in Release %2$s is not valid.
The app storage is not available.
An update is already in progress.
This canvasOS install does not have the Releases\' signature: update it once from a computer (AGENTS.md, step 3).
The Release file is too large (%1$d MB).
The downloaded file is over %1$d MB.
The file is incomplete (%1$d of %2$d bytes received).
The downloaded file is not an APK.
The downloaded file cannot be read.
